step12_scaling_decision: Full corporate treatment: a 5-yr 3-statement model (Assumptions -> P_and_L -> Balance_Sheet -> Credit_Ratios -> Debt_Breakup -> Stress_Case) plus the Step 12b scorecard. rating_outcome: CARE AA; Stable / CARE A1+ - reaffirmed. Assigned on: PBILDT margin 12.94% (FY2026) rising from 11.87%; PBILDT per tonne ~Rs 21,640 rising from ~Rs 19,630, which sits above CareEdge's own published ~Rs 20,000/tonne benchmark; gearing 0.42x on tangible net worth of Rs 17,900.83 crore; total debt/PBILDT 1.34x and net debt/PBILDT 0.81x; interest coverage 9.79x; RoCE 19.25% on average capital employed; liquidity Strong on Rs 2,931.60 crore of VERIFIED-unencumbered assets (Rs 3.55 crore under lien, checked not assumed). The Step 12b scorecard independently returns an anchor of AA, level with the assigned view. Contamination risk disclosed in GATES.md G10: CareEdge's own conclusion was necessarily seen at Step 7b because failure mode 29 requires the rated-amount table to be extracted before drafting and the grade sits in the same table. delivery_scope: Rationale in CareEdge press-release format (check_sections.py PASS, all quality probes clean) + ratio engine (26/26 tie-outs) + Financial_Spreads.xlsx (Extraction / RatioSuite / TieOut / Conventions, live formulas EVALUATED not just asserted) + 5yr_Model.xlsx (6 tabs, zero error cells, debt derived from the funding gap) + Rating_Scorecard (anchor AA) + verify_jsl.py (8 gates, 2 positive controls, all passing). CONSOLIDATED basis. Key figures: total operating income Rs 42,954.66 crore (FY2026, +9.3%), PBILDT Rs 5,560.43 crore (12.94%), PAT Rs 3,184.57 crore, total debt Rs 7,460.33 crore, sales volume ~2.57 MT (+8.1%).
method_notes: SIX real defects were caught mechanically and fixed against source, not tuned away. FIVE in the ratio engine: (1) FY2023 total equity missed non-controlling interest of 36.39 (11,931.18 vs the AR's 11,967.57); (2) FY2024 non-current assets typed as 15,934.24 against the file's own components summing to 16,034.64 - a 100.40 transcription error; (3) FY2025 non-current assets typed as 19,359.71 vs 19,359.74, which an earlier draft had wrongly written up as a '0.03 rounding difference between documents' when it was simply arithmetic - that false disclosure is withdrawn; (4) FY2025/26 current provisions read off a garbled table fragment as 66.55/60.67 against true figures of 6.65/6.07, a factor-of-ten misread; (5) the FY2025 Rs 7.06 crore Jindal Coke stake loss and FY2026 Rs 17.40 crore Ind AS 103 gain were being added back to PBILDT although note 39/40 shows both sit INSIDE exceptional items, which the base already excludes - a double-count that overstated FY2025 PBILDT. The engine was then restructured so NO subtotal is hard-coded: every total is summed from components and tied to the AR's printed row, making component-vs-total disagreement structurally impossible. A SIXTH was caught in the model: the first build hard-coded the two Balance_Sheet rows P_and_L references, a section header shifted the sheet by one, and projected finance costs came out ZERO for all five years while looking plausible - row anchors are now shared constants, build_bs asserts it wrote to them, and a gate independently asserts finance costs are positive in every projected year. PBILDT is built on CareEdge's OWN criteria, not ICRA's: non-debt forex is OPERATING and stays inside PBILDT, and on this issuer it needs no adjustment at all because the Other Expenses note shows a net GAIN in all four years already sitting in the base (see correction_2_26aug2026 - an earlier version wrongly restored a gain from Other Income, where no forex line exists); profit/loss on asset sales comes out, except a 11.61 crore FY2026 disposal loss that the notes do not isolate, which is left unadjusted and disclosed at 0.2% of PBILDT. The base reproduces the AR's OWN published EBITDA line to the paisa in both disclosed years (FY2025 4,666.63; FY2026 5,560.43) and the older AR's capital-management EBITDA once associate share and exceptional items are bridged back (FY2023 3,696.05; FY2024 4,856.57). Tangible net worth follows CareEdge's CORPORATE definition - intangibles excluded, deferred tax assets NOT deducted (that belongs to the financial-sector definition; carrying one across is failure mode 32); JSL's intangibles are mine development costs, software, customer relationships, trademarks and contracts, none of which fall in CareEdge's four critical-to-operations exceptions. Gearing is disclosed as UNADJUSTED because acceptances and group guarantees are not separately quantified in the consolidated accounts, which matters here since CareEdge's own sensitivities are framed on net debt INCLUDING acceptances. Three FALSE POSITIVES in the shared delivery gate were found by this case and fixed at source: the FM14 date probe accepted only day-first dates (CareEdge's own house format is month-first, so every correct CareEdge report would have failed forever), it triggered on the bare 'Press Release' masthead that opens every CareEdge rationale and could therefore never be satisfied, and it looked only forward for the date rather than both ways. Re-verified with a positive control and a full-corpus run identical to the pre-change baseline.
correction_2_26aug2026: Operator challenged the Brief Financials figures. Two real defects found. (1) THE FOREX LINE WAS THE WRONG FIGURE ENTIRELY: the engine carried [-15.57, 32.41, -70.04, 87.15], which are the "net unrealised foreign exchange (gain)/loss" rows from the CASH-FLOW RECONCILIATION, not the P&L line. The Other Expenses note (FY2025-26 note 34; FY2023-24 note 33) shows a NET GAIN in all four years - 68.48, 190.04, 154.37, 78.41 - so FY2026 had been entered as an 87.15 crore LOSS against an audited 78.41 crore GAIN, wrong in magnitude and direction. The add-back logic rested on a false premise (that the gain sat in Other Income and was stripped by "- other income"); note 29 decomposes Other Income fully and has no forex line at all. Since CareEdge treats non-debt forex as operating and it already sits in Other Expenses, NO add-back is warranted in any year; the false add-back had inflated FY2023 PBILDT by 15.57 and FY2025 by 70.04. Corrected: PBILDT FY2025 4,666.63 (was 4,736.67), FY2026 5,560.43 (was 5,572.04); margin 11.87%/12.94% (was 12.05%/12.97%); interest coverage 7.63x/9.79x; PBILDT per tonne ~19,630/~21,640. RoCE in the rationale corrected 21.43% -> 19.25% (the former was the model closing-CE measure quoted beside engine average-CE figures - an inconsistent basis). WHY THE TIE-OUTS MISSED IT: PBILDT was tied to the company published EBITDA, and the base reproduces that exactly whether or not a spurious add-back sits on top. The tie-outs verified the base; nothing verified the add-back. GENERAL LESSON: a cash-flow reconciliation line and a P&L note line are different measures of the same item, and only the note states what the P&L booked. (2) FOUR OF THE THEN-22 TIE-OUTS WERE CIRCULAR - the EPS checks compared a value to itself and could never fail, so "22/22" overstated the verification. Replaced with two genuinely independent checks per year (total income = revenue + other income; PAT owners + NCI = PAT). Now 26/26. THE RATING IS UNCHANGED at CARE AA; Stable / CARE A1+ - margin still improves, per-tonne economics still rise above CareEdge own ~20,000 benchmark, gearing untouched, scorecard anchor still AA. One narrative change: the "earnings swung violently in both directions" weakness was fiction and is withdrawn, replaced by the real and more material point that a persistent net forex gain worth up to 4.0% of PBILDT has more than halved since FY2024.
correction_3_26aug2026: Operator asked for the remaining report figures to be checked. audit_figures.py now classifies EVERY numeric token in the rationale as engine-reproducible (42), document-verbatim (86) or neither (19), and the 19 were verified by hand. ONE further real error found: the stress case asserted total debt/PBILDT of ~1.9x and interest coverage of ~4.1x, while the model computes 1.76x and 7.29x. The 4.1x had never been derived from anything - a naked assertion that understated stressed coverage by nearly half. Corrected in the rationale and the model read-across; the Stress_Case tab itself was right throughout, so this was prose drifting from computation. A new gate asserts the two agree, and its FIRST version passed its own positive control (it substring-matched "1.8"/"7.3" inside unrelated numbers like 11.87 and 7,460.33) and was rewritten until the control genuinely failed. All ESG and narrative figures spot-checked against the annual report and confirmed clean. Rating unchanged.
correction_4_26aug2026: Methodology change so the class of error cannot recur. Two failure modes added to CLAUDE.md, each with mechanical enforcement per the section 8a no-prose-only rule. FM38: a cash-flow reconciliation row is not a P&L line - the cash-flow row is the non-cash/unrealised adjustment, the note states what the P&L booked; enforced by preflight probe [0d] SAME ITEM IN TWO STATEMENTS, verified to print the 87.15/70.04 cash-flow row beside the note figures and name the conflict. FM39: counting tie-outs that pass is not measuring what they cover; enforced by the new reusable tieout_mutation.py plus case gate G12, which perturbs every input, reports those no check is sensitive to, and compares that set EXACTLY against an UNVERIFIED_INPUTS declaration in the engine. Acting on the harness took this case from 94.5% to 98.2% coverage by decomposing the Other Expenses note to its 25 line items and TYING them to the note printed total, and by tying the printed PBT waterfall step by step; tie-outs went 26 -> 39. The five remaining unverified inputs (EPS x4, FY2024 forex) are declared and feed no ratio. Generalisable rule now in ratio_template.py: FM36 requires decomposition, but decomposition is not verification - a decomposition must be tied back to the note own printed total. Corollary learned twice this session: a check that cannot fail its own positive control is not a check - both the stress-consistency gate and the first G12 passed their controls through substring coincidence and were rewritten until they genuinely failed. CORPUS FINDING not acted on here: Balkrishna Industries measures 13.4% coverage against its reported 18/18 tie-outs, because that engine hard-codes subtotals; flagged for separate work.
